articles.summary: There's something primordially satisfying about watching a big-screen dinosaur get the what-for from the business end of a just-loaded shotgun. The recent run of Jurassic Park movies sometimes seems to have lost this primal pleasure, replacing it with ho-hum computer-generated spectacle and cheap nostalgic callbacks to the franchise's better days. They've forgotten that the franchise was founded on a combination of awe and white-knuckle terror—the raw and relatable fear of a giant, toothy monster that stalks the earth with a sort of evolutionary arrogance that comes from a couple million years atop the food chain. Newsflash: Humans rule the planet now. It's fun to watch these ancient planetary powerhouses get taken down a peg. Sic semper Tyrannosaurus. stories.summary: Washington and Tehran again presented sharply contrasting narratives over the Strait of Hormuz, underscoring skepticism over the reopening of the waterway. Hours after US President Donald Trump said his forces had “total control” over Hormuz , Iranian officials said his remarks “ do not change the reality ” of its closure. The Wall Street Journal said tracking data showed just 14 ships traversed the channel on Tuesday, barely a tenth of pre-war levels , though a leading Bloomberg columnist suggested that analysts were likely underestimating the volume of oil crossing Hormuz: He noted that visible oil spills pointed to a battle between Iran trying to keep the strait closed while others push to keep it open, “ perhaps more successfully than we think .” — Prashant Rao

articles.summary: Iran’s recent reshuffle, as well as its shifting battlefield tactics, suggest it is adapting for a lengthening conflict with the US. Tehran has reordered its leadership in part because of repeated assassinations of its top brass by American and Israeli strikes. But recent moves point to how Iran is “ preparing for a prolonged confrontation ,” an expert wrote in Foreign Policy, noting that Iran was centralizing its military apparatus and increasing its focus on offensive operations.
